. Every data API has blind spots because each provider sees a different slice of the web, so I overlap as many providers as I could wire in and one covers what another misses.

I was also annoyed that deep research wasn’t durable, so Hyperresearch keeps every source a run reads and you can search it later and build on your research instead of starting over.

What’s in it:

   Research reports. Deep Search takes 3 to 5 hours across about 150 to 200 sources, and every cited claim is double-checked against its source before the report ships.

   A source vault. The sources a run reads stay in your workspace, searchable by words or meaning, from the console or MCP. [...] Add a card and your first Deep run is free.

What I'd love from you: give Answers a lookup your agent gets wrong today, and tell me whether it answered or said not_found, and whether that call was right.  
  
- Jordan

The lint gate catches structural failures (missing scaffold, broken provenance, unresolved CRITICALs). It cannot guarantee factual accuracy, that's still your call. [...] ```
# .hyperresearch/config.toml # web provider "crawl4ai" " "
```

Every fetch lane verifies TLS certificates by default: `builtin`, the PDF downloads, and crawl4ai's headless browser. A bad certificate fails the fetch with `CertVerificationError`; nothing retries it unverified. For a cert-broken site you trust, set the opt-out for the lane that refused it under `[fetch]`: `browser_verify_tls = false` for crawl4ai's headless browser, `pdf_verify_tls = false` for PDFs. The builtin provider has no opt-out. The visible-window browser used with a login profile (`--visible`, and the LinkedIn / Twitter-style domains) still accepts bad certificates, because some of the walled sites it exists for serve broken chains.

## Authenticated crawling + the browser lane [...] 250+ sources in a single run. The `premier` scale profile targets 100–130 in the width sweep alone; citation chasing and gap-fill fetches more than double what actually lands in the corpus.
 Every citation is verified before the report ships. A skeptical cite-checker audits whether each cited source actually supports its sentence. Hallucinated quotes and unacknowledged retractions are hard blocks at the gate.
 Syndication doesn't count as consensus. An independence audit clusters derivative copies, so five reprints of one press release argue with the weight of one source.
 Adversarial by construction. Four critics attack every draft in parallel, and a tool-locked patcher can only apply surgical edits. It physically cannot rewrite the report.

results.title: As Agentic AI Takes Center Stage, Concerns Surface
results.content:
Meanwhile, the technical reality of agentic shopping remains far from seamless. Maher, who has personally tested various agentic solutions, puts his current success rate at only around 70 percent. His experiences include agents purchasing items that were out of stock, failing to select appropriate shipping methods, and causing multi-week delays in delivery.

For a consumer, these are frustrating glitches, and for a retailer, they are the harbingers of a broken relationship. Maher warned that the "customer is always right" adage is being tested by this tsunami of AI, as users will likely direct their blame at both the AI provider and the brand when errors occur.
